page: Google Cloud Platform n4a-highmem-8 is an arm64-based virtual machine configuration featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 64 GB of system memory. Operating on an Arm architecture, this instance allocates 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, placing it in a high-memory tier that caters to workloads requiring expanded memory footprints relative to compute capacity. Hardware accelerator support is absent, with zero GPUs provisioned on this instance type.

The instance comes without bundled local storage, requiring attached persistent disk or network storage solutions for data persistence and operating system installations. Networking provisions include zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating Cloud NAT or independently allocated external IPs for direct public internet access. The lack of integrated NVMe drives represents an operational tradeoff for I/O-intensive pipelines that depend on low-latency local scratch disks, though the 1:8 core-to-memory ratio provides ample buffer for memory-resident working sets.

From a workload perspective, the 8-vCPU and 64 GB configuration is suited for medium-scale in-memory caching systems, transactional databases, JVM-based microservices, and memory-intensive ETL pipelines built for Arm64 environments. Deploying on Arm-based virtual hardware allows organizations to achieve high memory density with lower qualitative infrastructure overhead compared to traditional x86 alternatives, making it an efficient option for memory-bound tasks that do not demand graphics or tensor accelerators.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4a-highmem-8 is a memory-oriented virtual machine featuring 8 dedicated arm64 vCPUs and 64 GB of system RAM. With a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio providing 8.0 GB of memory per core, the configuration emphasizes memory capacity over dense compute. The instance includes no onboard local storage, depending entirely on attached network block storage, and offers no integrated GPU acceleration or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The underlying Arm architecture delivers cost-effective resource density for memory-bound workloads without requiring extreme parallel compute power. This hardware profile suits applications such as in-memory databases, Redis or Memcached instances, enterprise application runtimes, and intermediate data processing pipelines running on 64-bit Arm architectures.
